The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information (stored as timestamptz in database). A null value indicates the user has never logged in since account creation, which would only occur on the very first login.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was originally created.

This is the created_at field from either discussion_board_members or discussion_board_moderators table. An immutable field set automatically during account registration. Used for calculating account age, displaying 'member since' information, sorting users by join date, and audit trail purposes.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, representing the exact moment the user record was inserted into the database.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the user profile was last modified.

This is the updated_at field from either discussion_board_members or discussion_board_moderators table. Automatically updated whenever any user account information changes, including profile edits, password changes, privacy setting updates, or status changes. Helps track account maintenance activity and identify recently updated profiles.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information, representing the most recent modification to any field in the user record.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the user account.

This is the deleted_at field from either discussion_board_members or discussion_board_moderators table. When a user deletes their account, this field is set to the deletion timestamp rather than immediately removing the record. This enables account recovery during a grace period, maintains referential integrity for authored articles and comments, and preserves audit trail for moderation records.

A null value indicates the account is active. A non-null value would indicate the account is soft-deleted, though in practice this field should always be null in successful login responses since deleted accounts cannot authenticate.

moderation_permissions.description:
JSON string defining specific moderation permissions and access levels.

This is the moderation_permissions field from the discussion_board_moderators table. Only populated when the authenticated user is a moderator (role equals 'moderator'). Null for member users as this field does not exist in the discussion_board_members table.

The JSON structure specifies granular moderation capabilities such as can_edit_articles, can_delete_articles, can_edit_comments, can_delete_comments, can_issue_warnings, can_suspend_users, can_ban_users, can_manage_reports, and can_manage_categories. These permissions determine which moderation actions the moderator can perform and are checked at the application layer when moderators attempt to execute enforcement operations.

token.description:
JWT token information for session authentication.

This object contains both the access token and refresh token required for maintaining an authenticated session. The access token is a short-lived JWT (30-minute expiration) included in the Authorization header of API requests to prove user identity and permissions. The refresh token is a longer-lived JWT (30-day expiration) used to obtain new access tokens when the current access token expires, enabling seamless session continuation without requiring the user to re-enter credentials.

Both tokens are cryptographically signed using the server's secret key and contain claims such as user ID, role, and expiration timestamps. The client must store these tokens securely and use them according to the authentication flow defined in the system requirements.

success.description:
Indicates whether the logout operation completed successfully.

When true, the member or moderator session has been properly terminated by setting the expired_at timestamp in the respective session table (discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions). The refresh token associated with this session has been invalidated and can no longer be used to obtain new access tokens.

The client application must discard both the access token and refresh token from local storage upon receiving a successful logout response to complete the logout process on the client side.

message.description:
Human-readable confirmation message describing the logout result.

Provides user-friendly feedback about the session termination, such as 'Logout successful' or 'Your session has been ended'. This message can be displayed to users to confirm their logout action was processed.

The message maintains a consistent, professional tone appropriate for an economic and political discussion board platform.

IDiscussionBoardAuth.ILogoutResult.description:
Response confirming successful termination of an authenticated user session.

This type represents the result of a logout operation for either a member or moderator actor. When logout succeeds, the system has marked the current session as expired in the database by setting the expired_at timestamp, preventing the refresh token from being reused to obtain new access tokens.

The logout operation only affects the current device's session - users may remain logged in on other devices if they have multiple active sessions. The operation extracts session information from the JWT access token, so no request parameters are needed. After logout, users must perform fresh authentication (login) to regain access to protected features.

This response type is returned by both the member logout operation (POST /discussionBoard/member/auth/logout) and the moderator logout operation (POST /discussionBoard/moderator/auth/logout), providing a consistent logout experience across different user actor types.

refresh_token.description:
Current refresh token to exchange for new access token.

This is the refresh token that was previously issued during login or the last token refresh operation. The token is associated with an active session record in the discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions table.

The refresh token serves as proof of an existing authenticated session and authorizes the issuance of a new access token without requiring the user to re-enter their username and password. This enables seamless session continuation when the short-lived access token (30-minute validity) expires.

Token validation process: The system validates this refresh token by checking its signature and expiration (typically 14-30 days validity), verifying the associated session exists in the database and has not been explicitly expired (expired_at field is null or in the future), confirming the user account is still active (status field is 'active' in discussion_board_members or discussion_board_moderators table), and ensuring the session has not been invalidated due to security events (password changes, suspicious activity, or explicit logout).

Security considerations: Refresh tokens are long-lived credentials that should be stored securely by clients (httpOnly cookies or secure client storage), never exposed in URLs, logs, or client-side JavaScript accessible locations, transmitted only over HTTPS connections, and invalidated immediately when users log out or change passwords.

Clients should implement token refresh logic that proactively refreshes access tokens before expiration (within 5 minutes of expiry) or reactively refreshes when receiving 401 Unauthorized responses, handles refresh failures by redirecting to login, and manages token storage securely across application restarts.

IDiscussionBoardAuth.IRefresh.description:
Request payload for refreshing authentication tokens to maintain active session.

This request is submitted when a client needs to obtain a new access token because the current access token has expired or is about to expire. Token refresh is a fundamental part of modern authentication systems that balance security (short-lived access tokens) with user experience (long-lived sessions without repeated logins).

Authentication architecture context: The discussion board uses JWT (JSON Web Token) based authentication with two token types serving different purposes. Access tokens are short-lived (30 minutes) and included in every authenticated API request via the Authorization header, containing user identity and permission claims. Refresh tokens are long-lived (14-30 days) and used exclusively for obtaining new access tokens, not for direct API authentication, with each token associated with a database session record.

The refresh token provided in this request must be valid, unexpired, and associated with an active user session. The system validates the token and session state by querying the session tables (discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions), checking the session's created_at and expired_at timestamps, and verifying the associated user account status.

Successful refresh operation: When validation succeeds, the system generates a new access token with fresh 30-minute expiration, optionally rotates the refresh token for enhanced security (issuing a new refresh token and invalidating the old one), updates the session record if token rotation occurs, and returns the new token set to the client for continued authenticated access.

Failure scenarios: Token refresh fails when the refresh token is expired (beyond its validity period), the associated session has been explicitly expired (expired_at field is set), the user account is suspended, deleted, or otherwise inactive (status field check), the refresh token has been invalidated due to password change or security event, or the token signature is invalid or the token has been tampered with.

Client implementation: Clients should call this endpoint when the access token expires or is about to expire, handle refresh failures by redirecting users to login, implement automatic retry logic for transient failures, and maintain security by protecting the refresh token in secure storage.

access_token.description:
JWT access token for authenticated API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header of all subsequent API requests requiring authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user ID, role (member or moderator), username, and email verification status.

The access token has a 30-minute validity period from the time of issuance. After expiration, clients should use the refresh operation to obtain a new access token without requiring the user to re-enter credentials.

Format: Bearer token following JWT (JSON Web Token) standard, signed with HS256 algorithm. Clients should store this token securely and include it in the Authorization header as 'Bearer {access_token}' for authenticated requests.

token_type.description:
Token type indicator for HTTP Authorization header.

This field always contains the value 'Bearer', indicating that the access_token should be used as a Bearer token in the Authorization header of HTTP requests.

Clients should construct the Authorization header as: 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}'

expires_in.description:
Access token expiration time in seconds.

Indicates how many seconds from the time of issuance the access token will remain valid. For this system, access tokens expire after 1800 seconds (30 minutes).

Clients can use this value to determine when to refresh the token proactively, ensuring seamless user experience by refreshing before expiration rather than waiting for authentication errors.

refresh_token.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token enables users to obtain new access tokens when the current access token expires, without requiring re-authentication with username and password. The refresh token is used with the token refresh operation.

The refresh token has a longer validity period than the access token (typically 14-30 days) and should be stored securely by the client. When the access token expires, clients should call the refresh endpoint with this token to receive a new access token.

Security considerations: Refresh tokens should be stored securely (httpOnly cookies or secure client storage), never exposed in URLs or logs, and invalidated when the user explicitly logs out or changes their password. Each refresh token is associated with a specific session record in the database (discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions table).

IDiscussionBoardAuth.ITokens.description:
Authentication tokens issued upon successful login or token refresh.

This response contains all tokens necessary for maintaining an authenticated session in the discussion board system. The structure follows OAuth 2.0 token response conventions with JWT (JSON Web Token) implementation for stateless authentication.

The access token provides short-term authentication for API requests and expires after 30 minutes to limit the window of vulnerability if compromised. The refresh token provides long-term session maintenance, allowing users to obtain new access tokens without re-entering credentials, with validity typically lasting 14-30 days.

Clients should implement token management logic that stores both tokens securely, includes the access token in all authenticated requests, monitors token expiration, and uses the refresh token to obtain new access tokens before or immediately after the access token expires.

Security model: The system uses JWT tokens signed with HS256 algorithm, with access tokens containing user identity and permission claims. Session state is tracked in the database through session tables (discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions), allowing session invalidation when users log out, change passwords, or when suspicious activity is detected.

token.description:
Email verification token received in the verification email during registration.

This is a unique, cryptographically secure token with 24-hour validity that confirms email ownership. The token is generated when a user registers and sent to their email address. It must be provided exactly as received in the verification email link.

The token is validated through application logic using a secure token service or cache layer, as verification tokens are not stored in the Prisma database tables.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.
IP address not provided by client (server will extract from request).

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.

This field is OPTIONAL and can be provided by the client for server-side rendering (SSR) scenarios where the actual client IP needs to be forwarded. When not provided (null or undefined), the backend server automatically extracts the IP address from the HTTP request headers.

The IP address is used for security monitoring, rate limiting, and session management when the user is automatically logged in after successful email verification. It populates the ip field in the discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions table.

For direct browser-to-server connections, clients typically omit this field and let the server detect the IP. For SSR scenarios, the application server should provide the actual client IP to ensure accurate session tracking.

href.description:
Connection URL where the email verification was performed.

This is the MANDATORY current page URL from which the user is verifying their email address. It represents the complete URL of the verification page or component, including protocol, domain, path, and any query parameters.

The href value is used for session tracking, analytics, and security purposes when creating the initial authenticated session after successful verification. It populates the href field in the discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions table.

For single-page applications (SPAs), this should be the current browser URL. For verification links that open in email clients or browsers, this is the landing page URL where verification completes.

Example values:
- 'https://discussion.example.com/verify-email?token=xyz'
- 'https://discussion.example.com/auth/verify'
- 'https://discussion.example.com/welcome?verified=true'

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the email verification page.

This is the MANDATORY previous page URL from which the user navigated to complete email verification. It represents the page the user was viewing before clicking the verification link in their email or before navigating to the verification interface.

The referrer value is used for analytics and understanding user verification flows. It populates the referrer field in the discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions table when the initial session is created upon successful verification.

For verification links clicked directly from email clients, this may be the email client identifier or an empty string. For web-based email clients, this would be the webmail URL.

Example values:
- 'https://mail.google.com/' (clicked verification link from Gmail)
- 'https://discussion.example.com/' (navigated from homepage to verification)
- '' (empty string for direct link access from native email clients)

IDiscussionBoardAuth.IVerifyEmail.description:
Email verification request containing the verification token from the registration email.

This request body is used to verify a user's email address and activate their account after registration. Email verification is a mandatory step in the user registration workflow that confirms the user has access to the provided email address.

This is a SELF-AUTHENTICATION operation where the user themselves is verifying their email and establishing their first authenticated session. Upon successful verification, the system automatically logs in the user and creates a session record in discussion_board_member_sessions or discussion_board_moderator_sessions. Therefore, session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are REQUIRED to populate the session table.

The verification token is sent to the user's email address during registration and must be submitted to this operation to complete account activation. Upon successful verification, the user's account transitions from pending_email_verification status to active status, and the email_verified field is set to true in the discussion_board_members or discussion_board_moderators table.

The href and referrer fields are MANDATORY as they capture the verification context and cannot be inferred server-side. The ip field is OPTIONAL since the server can extract it from the HTTP request, but clients MAY provide it for SSR scenarios.

This operation is part of the authentication flow and does not require prior authentication, as it occurs before the user can log in. However, it results in immediate authentication and session creation upon success.

success.description:
Indicates whether email verification was successful.

When true, the user's email has been verified, their account status has been updated from pending_email_verification to active, and the email_verified field has been set to true in the database. The user can now log in and access full platform features.

When false, verification failed due to invalid token, expired token, or other validation issues.

message.description:
Human-readable message explaining the verification result.

For successful verification, this message confirms account activation and may provide next steps such as logging in. For failed verification, this message explains what went wrong and how to resolve the issue, such as requesting a new verification email if the token expired.

Messages follow user-friendly error message standards, providing clear explanations and actionable guidance without technical jargon.

token.description:
JWT authentication tokens for immediate login after successful email verification.

Provided only when verification is successful, enabling the user to access the platform immediately without requiring a separate login step. Contains both access token (30-minute expiration) and refresh token (14-day expiration) following the JWT authentication requirements.

This field is null or omitted when verification fails.

IDiscussionBoardAuth.IVerificationResult.description:
Result of email verification operation indicating success status and providing authentication tokens for immediate login.

This response is returned after validating an email verification token. When verification succeeds, the user's account is activated by updating the email_verified field to true and changing the account status from pending_email_verification to active in the discussion_board_members or discussion_board_moderators table.

Successful verification includes authentication tokens enabling immediate login without requiring the user to manually enter credentials. This streamlines the user experience by allowing newly registered users to begin using the platform immediately after email verification.

The response includes a success boolean indicating verification outcome, a user-friendly message explaining the result and next steps, and JWT tokens for authenticated access when verification succeeds. If verification fails due to invalid or expired tokens, the response indicates failure and provides guidance on requesting a new verification email.

email.description:
Email address of the account for which password reset is requested.

This is the email address registered with the user account. The system will send password reset instructions to this email if an account exists with this address.

For security reasons, the system returns the same success message regardless of whether this email exists in the database, preventing email enumeration attacks.

IDiscussionBoardPasswordReset.IRequest.description:
Password reset request data structure for initiating the password recovery process.

This request body is used when a user has forgotten their password and needs to reset it. The user provides their registered email address, and the system generates a secure password reset token and sends instructions via email.

The operation implements security measures including rate limiting (one request per 5 minutes per email) and email enumeration protection (identical response whether email exists or not).

message.description:
Generic success message indicating that password reset instructions have been sent if an account exists.

This message is intentionally vague for security purposes, not revealing whether the provided email address actually exists in the system. The standard message is: 'If an account exists with this email, you will receive password reset instructions.'

This prevents malicious actors from using the password reset function to enumerate valid email addresses registered in the system.

IDiscussionBoardPasswordReset.IRequestRe.description:
Response message for password reset request operation.

This response confirms that the password reset request was processed. For security reasons, it provides the same success message regardless of whether the email address exists in the system, preventing email enumeration attacks.

If an account exists with the provided email, a password reset email with a unique token is sent to that address. The token expires after 2 hours and is single-use only.

token.description:
Password reset token received via email.

This is the unique, cryptographically secure token that was generated during the password reset request operation and sent to the user's email address. The token must be valid, not expired (2-hour expiration), and not previously used.

The token authenticates this password reset request and ensures that only the legitimate account owner who has access to the registered email can reset the password.

new_password.description:
New password to set for the user account.

This password must meet all security complexity requirements including minimum 8 characters length, at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), at least one lowercase letter (a-z), at least one number (0-9), and at least one special character (e.g., !@#$%^&*).

The password is validated against common compromised password databases and rejected if it matches known breached passwords. The system securely hashes this password before storing it in the password_hash field.

password_confirmation.description:
Confirmation of the new password to prevent typos.

This field must exactly match the new_password field. If the values do not match, the system rejects the password reset request and displays an error message.

Requiring password confirmation reduces the risk of users accidentally setting a password they didn't intend due to typing errors.

IDiscussionBoardPasswordReset.IConfirm.description:
Password reset confirmation data structure for completing the password recovery process.

This request body is used in the second step of password reset, after the user has received the reset token via email and clicked the reset link. The user provides the token, their desired new password, and password confirmation.

Upon successful validation and password update, all existing user sessions are invalidated, forcing the user to log in again from all devices with the new password. This security measure ensures that if an unauthorized party had access to the account, they are immediately logged out when the legitimate owner resets the password.

message.description:
Success confirmation message indicating the password was successfully reset.

This message provides immediate feedback to the user that their password change was completed successfully. The message reassures users that their account is now secured with the new password and prompts them to log in using the updated credentials.

Typical message content confirms the password reset completion, informs the user that all existing sessions have been invalidated for security purposes, and directs them to the login page to authenticate with their new password.

IDiscussionBoardPasswordReset.IConfirmRe.description:
Response confirming successful password reset completion.

This response is returned when a user successfully completes the password reset process by validating their reset token and setting a new password. The response confirms that the password has been updated in the discussion_board_members table, all existing sessions have been invalidated, and a confirmation email has been sent.

The password reset confirmation response provides essential feedback to users who have completed the account recovery process. It reassures them that their account is now secured with the new password and guides them toward the next step of logging in with their updated credentials.

This response marks the successful conclusion of the two-step password recovery flow, which begins with a password reset request that generates and emails a reset token, and concludes with this confirmation operation that validates the token and applies the new password.

title.description:
Article title or headline.

Required title for the article, between 5 and 200 characters. The title should be descriptive and clearly convey the article's topic. The system trims leading and trailing whitespace and validates that the title contains meaningful content rather than only special characters or numbers.

body.description:
Main article content and body text.

Required full text content of the article, between 20 and 50,000 characters. This field contains the complete article with rich text formatting. The system preserves paragraph breaks and basic formatting while sanitizing HTML input to prevent XSS attacks and other security vulnerabilities.

summary.description:
Optional article excerpt or summary.

An optional brief summary or excerpt, limited to 500 characters. When provided, this summary is used in article previews, listings, and search results. If omitted or set to null, the system may automatically generate a preview from the beginning of the article body.

category_ids.description:
Category classifications for this article.

Array of category IDs from the discussion_board_categories table. At least one category is required to classify the article's subject matter (e.g., Economic Policy, Political Analysis). Articles can belong to multiple categories for flexible organization. The system validates that all referenced categories exist before article creation.

tag_ids.description:
Optional topic tags for enhanced discoverability.

Array of tag IDs from the discussion_board_tags table providing granular topic keywords (e.g., monetary-policy, healthcare-reform). Maximum 5 tags allowed per article. Tags are optional but recommended for improved content discovery. The system validates that all referenced tags exist.

image_ids.description:
Image attachments for visual evidence and supporting materials.

Array of pre-uploaded image IDs from the discussion_board_article_images table. Images must be uploaded via a separate file upload endpoint before article creation. Maximum 10 images allowed per article, each with a maximum size of 5MB. Supported formats include JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP.

document_ids.description:
Document attachments for supplementary materials and research.

Array of pre-uploaded document IDs from the discussion_board_article_documents table. Documents must be uploaded via a separate file upload endpoint before article creation. Maximum 5 documents allowed per article, each with a maximum size of 10MB. Supported formats include PDF, DOCX, DOC, TXT, RTF, and ODT.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate.description:
Article creation request for publishing new discussion board content.

This type defines the structure for creating new articles in the discussion board system. It includes all user-provided content and metadata necessary to publish economic and political discussions with supporting evidence through multimedia attachments.

The creation process validates all required fields according to business rules. Title must be between 5 and 200 characters, body content must be between 20 and 50,000 characters, and at least one category must be selected from the discussion_board_categories table. Optional fields include summary (max 500 characters, nullable), tags (max 5 from discussion_board_tags), image attachments (max 10 pre-uploaded images), and document attachments (max 5 pre-uploaded documents).

Authentication context from the JWT token automatically provides the author identification, so discussion_board_member_id is NOT included in this request body - it is populated server-side from the authenticated user's session. This prevents security vulnerabilities where users could impersonate other members.

System-generated fields excluded from this creation request include the article ID (generated by the system), view_count and comment_count (initialized to 0 automatically), created_at and updated_at timestamps (set by the system), and last_modified_by_moderator_id (null for new articles). The status field is automatically set to 'published' for immediate publication.

Attachment handling follows a two-phase process where files are first uploaded to temporary storage via dedicated file upload endpoints, receiving unique IDs that are then referenced in this article creation request. This separation allows file validation and processing before article submission and supports better error handling and user experience.

url.description:
Pre-uploaded image file URL from storage service.

The complete URL where the image file has been uploaded and stored. This URL points to the actual image file in the storage system (S3, CDN, or file server) and must be accessible by the backend for validation and processing. The image at this URL will be validated for format, dimensions, and content before being associated with the article.

original_name.description:
Original filename of the image as provided by the user.

The filename that the image had when the user selected it for upload (e.g., 'budget_chart_2024.png', 'trade_data.jpg'). This human-readable name helps users identify their uploaded files and is displayed in the article's attachment list. The system preserves this original name for user convenience while generating a unique stored_name for actual file storage.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the image file for validation and content delivery.

Specifies the image format using standard MIME type notation. Must be one of the supported image formats: 'image/jpeg' for JPEG/JPG files, 'image/png' for PNG files, 'image/gif' for GIF files (including animated), or 'image/webp' for WebP files. The system validates that the MIME type matches the actual file content at the provided URL, not just the file extension, to prevent format spoofing and ensure proper content handling.

size_bytes.description:
File size of the image in bytes.

The total size of the image file measured in bytes. This value is validated to ensure it does not exceed the 5MB (5,242,880 bytes) maximum limit for individual image attachments. The size is checked during upload validation and is stored for display to users (showing file sizes helps users make informed decisions about downloading on metered connections).

width.description:
Image width in pixels for dimension validation.

The horizontal dimension of the image in pixels. Must be at least 50 pixels (minimum readable size) and cannot exceed 8000 pixels (maximum practical size). This dimension is validated during upload to ensure images are suitable for display and do not cause performance issues. The width is used for generating appropriately sized thumbnails and responsive image variants.

height.description:
Image height in pixels for dimension validation.

The vertical dimension of the image in pixels. Must be at least 50 pixels (minimum readable size) and cannot exceed 8000 pixels (maximum practical size). Combined with width, this provides the complete aspect ratio for proper image display, thumbnail generation, and layout calculations. The height is validated during upload to ensure images meet quality and performance standards.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for uploading a new image attachment to a discussion board article.

This schema defines the data structure required when authenticated members or moderators upload image attachments to articles. Following AutoBE's URL-only file upload pattern, clients must first upload the image file to the storage service (S3, CDN, etc.) to obtain a URL, then submit that URL along with file metadata in this request.

The system validates all provided metadata against the file at the given URL to ensure consistency and security. File type validation confirms the MIME type matches the actual file content, not just the extension. Size validation ensures the image is within the 5MB maximum limit. Dimension validation checks that the image meets minimum readable size (50x50 pixels) and does not exceed maximum practical size (8000x8000 pixels). The system also verifies that adding this image will not cause the article to exceed the maximum of 10 total image attachments.

Important security considerations: The uploaded_by_member_id is automatically captured from the authenticated user's JWT token and must never be included in this request body. The article ID is provided via the path parameter, not in the request body. The stored_name is generated by the backend to ensure uniqueness and security, so it is not part of the request.

This two-phase upload approach (first upload file to get URL, then submit metadata) separates file storage concerns from business logic, enables pre-upload validation, supports multiple storage providers, prevents payload size issues in JSON requests, allows file reuse across entities, and maintains clean, testable business APIs.

url.description:
Pre-uploaded document file URL from storage service.

The complete URL where the document file has been uploaded and stored. This URL points to the actual document file in the storage system (S3, CDN, or file server) and must be accessible by the backend for validation and processing. The document at this URL will be validated for format and content before being associated with the article.

Following AutoBE's URL-only file upload pattern, clients must first upload the document file to the storage service through a separate file upload endpoint to obtain this URL. The backend then uses this URL to retrieve the file for validation, security scanning, and permanent storage association with the article.

original_name.description:
Original filename of the document being uploaded.

This should be the actual filename from the user's file system (e.g., 'Federal_Reserve_Report_2024.pdf', 'Economic_Analysis.docx', 'Policy_Brief.txt'). The filename helps users and readers identify the document's content at a glance and is preserved for display purposes in the article view. The system will generate a separate unique stored filename for internal storage while preserving this original name for user-facing displays.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the document file indicating its format.

Must be one of the supported document MIME types: 'application/pdf' for PDF documents, 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document' for DOCX files, 'application/msword' for older DOC files, 'text/plain' for TXT files, 'application/rtf' for Rich Text Format, or 'application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text' for ODT files. The MIME type is validated against both the file extension and actual file content to prevent format spoofing and ensure proper file handling.

size_bytes.description:
File size of the document in bytes.

Must be provided to enable validation against the maximum document size limit of 10MB (10,485,760 bytes) and the total attachment size limit of 100MB per article. The size is measured in bytes for precision and is also displayed to users in human-readable format (KB, MB) to help them make informed decisions about downloads, especially on limited bandwidth connections. Files under 1 byte or over 10MB are rejected.

IDiscussionBoardArticleDocument.ICreate.description:
Request payload for uploading and attaching a document file to a discussion board article.

This DTO represents the information needed to create a new document attachment record after a document file has been uploaded to storage. The document upload follows AutoBE's standardized two-phase pattern: first, the actual file is uploaded to the storage service (S3, CDN, file system) through a dedicated file upload endpoint which returns the file URL; second, this DTO is submitted with the URL and metadata to create the database record linking the uploaded file to the article.

The two-phase approach separates file storage concerns from business logic, enables pre-upload validation and virus scanning, supports multiple storage providers without API changes, prevents payload size issues in JSON requests, allows file reuse across entities, and maintains clean, testable business APIs. This pattern is identical to the image upload workflow for consistency across all file attachment types.

The DTO excludes certain fields that are automatically managed by the system. The document ID is auto-generated upon creation. The parent article ID comes from the path parameter (articleId in the URL). The uploader's member ID is automatically captured from the authenticated user's JWT token - clients should never provide this value as it would enable impersonation attacks. The creation timestamp is automatically set by the database. The deleted_at field is always null on creation as documents start in an active state. The stored_name is generated by the backend to ensure uniqueness and security.

Validation rules enforced by this DTO include: url must be a valid URI pointing to an accessible document file, original filename must be provided and cannot be empty, MIME type must match one of the supported document formats (PDF, DOCX, DOC, TXT, RTF, ODT), file size must be between 1 byte and 10MB (10,485,760 bytes), and the total size of all attachments on the parent article (including this document) must not exceed 100MB.

Security considerations are critical for this operation. The uploaded_by_member_id is never accepted in the request body - it is always derived from the authenticated user's session token to prevent members from uploading documents under other users' identities. The article ID in the path parameter is validated to ensure the authenticated member is the article author or a moderator before allowing document attachment. File content at the provided URL is validated and scanned for malware before the stored_name is generated, ensuring only safe files are referenced in this DTO.

This DTO supports the platform's core value proposition of evidence-based discussion by enabling users to attach authoritative documents, research papers, policy briefs, and data files directly to their economic and political analysis articles, making supporting evidence immediately accessible to readers.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the article.

This is the primary key automatically generated by the system when the article is created. It uniquely identifies this article across the entire discussion board system and is used in URLs, API references, and all relationships with other entities.

discussion_board_member_id.description:
Author member who created this article.

This foreign key references the discussion_board_members.id field and identifies which member account authored and published this article. The member ID is automatically populated from the authenticated user's JWT token during article creation, never accepted from client input to prevent impersonation attacks.

This field establishes ownership of the article, determining who has permission to edit or delete the content. Only the original author or moderators can modify articles. The author relationship is immutable after article creation - ownership cannot be transferred to other members.

The author member ID is used to enforce access control rules, attribute content to the correct user in article displays and listings, populate the author relationship for displaying member profile information, and maintain referential integrity with the discussion_board_members table through cascade deletion rules.

last_modified_by_moderator_id.description:
Moderator who last modified this article, if applicable.

This optional foreign key references discussion_board_moderators.id and tracks when a moderator edits an article that was originally created by a member. When an article author (member) edits their own article, this field remains null. When a moderator edits any article regardless of original authorship, this field is set to the moderator's ID.

This tracking field serves multiple critical purposes in the moderation system. It provides transparency to the community about which content has been modified by moderators versus authors, supports moderation audit trails by identifying moderator interventions in user-generated content, enables moderation action logging and accountability, and helps distinguish between author edits and moderator edits in version history.

The field is nullable because most articles are edited only by their original authors and never require moderator intervention. When populated, it indicates that platform administrators have reviewed and modified the content, which may be disclosed to readers through 'Edited by Moderator' indicators in the user interface.

This field is updated each time a moderator edits the article, always reflecting the most recent moderator who made changes. If multiple moderators edit an article over time, only the most recent moderator's ID is retained in this field, though the complete edit history is preserved in the discussion_board_article_snapshots table.

title.description:
Article title or headline.

The article title must be between 5 and 200 characters long, providing enough space for descriptive headlines while preventing excessive length. Titles are prominently displayed in article listings, search results, and on the article detail page. The system trims leading and trailing whitespace and prevents titles consisting only of special characters or numbers.

body.description:
Main article content and body text.

The full text content of the article must be between 20 and 50,000 characters. This field contains the complete article text with preserved formatting including paragraph breaks and basic text structure. The system sanitizes HTML input to prevent security vulnerabilities while preserving user-intended formatting such as line breaks and paragraphs.

summary.description:
Optional article excerpt or summary.

An optional brief summary or excerpt of the article, limited to 500 characters maximum. When provided, this summary is used in article previews, listings, and search results to give readers a quick overview of the article content. If not provided, the system may use the first portion of the article body for preview purposes.

oneOf.description:
Publication status of the article.

Indicates the current lifecycle state of the article. Values include 'published' for publicly visible articles, 'draft' for unpublished work-in-progress content, and 'archived' for older content that has been removed from primary circulation but retained for historical purposes. Only published articles appear in public listings and search results.

Publication status of the article.

Indicates the current lifecycle state of the article. Values include 'published' for publicly visible articles, 'draft' for unpublished work-in-progress content, and 'archived' for older content that has been removed from primary circulation but retained for historical purposes. Only published articles appear in public listings and search results.

Publication status of the article.

Indicates the current lifecycle state of the article. Values include 'published' for publicly visible articles, 'draft' for unpublished work-in-progress content, and 'archived' for older content that has been removed from primary circulation but retained for historical purposes. Only published articles appear in public listings and search results.

status.description:
Publication status of the article.

Indicates the current lifecycle state of the article. Values include 'published' for publicly visible articles, 'draft' for unpublished work-in-progress content, and 'archived' for older content that has been removed from primary circulation but retained for historical purposes. Only published articles appear in public listings and search results.

view_count.description:
Number of times this article has been viewed.

A system-managed counter that increments each time a user accesses the article detail page. This metric helps identify popular content and provides engagement statistics. The count is initialized to 0 when an article is created and is automatically incremented by the system on each article view.

comment_count.description:
Cached count of comments on this article.

A system-managed counter tracking the total number of comments (including both top-level comments and replies) associated with this article. This count is initialized to 0 when the article is created and is automatically updated when comments are added or removed. The cached count enables efficient display of engagement metrics without requiring expensive database queries.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the article was originally created.

Records the exact date and time when this article was first published to the discussion board. This timestamp is immutable after creation and serves as the primary sorting criterion for article chronological ordering. It provides historical context and helps users understand the timeliness of the content.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the article was last modified.

Records the most recent date and time when any aspect of the article was updated, including title changes, body content edits, metadata updates, or attachment modifications. This field is automatically updated by the system on each edit operation and helps readers identify recently revised content.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the article.

When an article is deleted by its author or a moderator, this field is set to the deletion timestamp rather than permanently removing the record from the database. A null value indicates the article is active and publicly accessible. A non-null timestamp indicates the article has been soft-deleted and should be hidden from public view.

Soft deletion provides several critical capabilities. It enables content recovery if articles are deleted in error or if moderation decisions are reversed. It maintains referential integrity for comments, snapshots, attachments, and moderation logs that reference the article. It preserves audit trails showing when content was removed and by whom. It supports compliance with data retention policies and legal requirements for content tracking.

When deleted_at is set, the article is excluded from public search results, category browsing, and article listings. However, moderators may retain access to deleted articles for audit and investigation purposes. The article's associated comments are typically hidden along with the article to maintain discussion coherence.

The deletion timestamp works in conjunction with the article's status field. Typically, articles are marked as deleted through the deleted_at timestamp rather than changing the status field, though implementation may vary. The updated_at timestamp is also updated when deletion occurs to reflect the most recent change to the article record.

author.description:
Member who created this article.

Reference to the author's member account providing context about who published this content. The author information includes public profile fields such as username, display name, and profile picture for proper attribution and credibility. The relationship is established through the discussion_board_member_id foreign key in the articles table.

lastModifiedByModerator.description:
Moderator who last modified this article, if applicable.

When a moderator edits an article (rather than the original author), this field references the moderator's account to track moderator intervention. This provides transparency about content that has been modified by platform administrators and supports moderation audit trails. The field is null for articles that have only been edited by their original authors.

categories.description:
Categories assigned to this article for organization and discovery.

A collection of predefined topic categories (e.g., Economic Policy, Political Analysis) that classify this article's subject matter. Articles must have at least one category and can belong to multiple categories for flexible organization. Categories enable users to browse related articles and filter content by topic area.

tags.description:
Flexible topic tags for detailed article labeling.

User-generated keywords that provide granular topic classification beyond formal categories. Tags enable detailed content filtering and discovery (e.g., monetary-policy, climate-change, taxation). Articles can have up to 5 tags, each normalized to lowercase for consistency. Tags are optional but highly recommended for improved discoverability.

images.description:
Image attachments associated with this article.

Collection of images uploaded as supporting visual content including charts, graphs, infographics, and photographs. Each image includes metadata such as original filename, dimensions, file size, and storage information. Images are displayed inline within the article view and can be viewed at full resolution. Maximum 10 images per article with 5MB maximum per image.

documents.description:
Document attachments associated with this article.

Collection of document files uploaded as supplementary materials including research papers, policy documents, and data files. Each document includes metadata such as original filename, MIME type, and file size. Documents are presented as downloadable links with file type indicators. Maximum 5 documents per article with 10MB maximum per document.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:
Complete article entity representing a discussion board article with all content, metadata, and relationships.

This is the primary content type in the discussion board system, representing economic and political analysis, commentary, and discussions published by members and moderators. Articles contain rich text content with support for formatting, multiple category and tag classifications for organization, and multimedia attachments including images and documents for evidence-based discussions.

Articles are created by members (tracked via discussion_board_member_id) and can be edited by their authors or by moderators (tracked via last_modified_by_moderator_id). Each article maintains a complete version history through the discussion_board_article_snapshots table, enabling audit trails and potential rollback capabilities.

The article lifecycle supports multiple statuses including published (publicly visible), draft (work in progress), and archived (removed from circulation). Articles use soft deletion (deleted_at timestamp) allowing content recovery and maintaining data integrity for audit purposes.

Engagement is tracked through system-managed counters including view_count (incremented on each article access) and comment_count (updated when comments are added or removed). These metrics provide insights into article popularity and discussion activity without requiring expensive real-time calculations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the image attachment.

This is the primary key generated by the system when the image is uploaded and stored in the discussion_board_article_images table. The ID uniquely identifies this image attachment across the entire system and is used for all subsequent operations on this image (retrieval, deletion, management).

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Reference to the parent article that this image is attached to.

This foreign key establishes the ownership relationship between the image and its parent article in the discussion_board_articles table. Every image must belong to exactly one article, and this association is immutable once created. When the parent article is deleted, all associated images are automatically deleted (cascade delete).

uploaded_by_member_id.description:
Member who uploaded this image attachment.

This foreign key references the discussion_board_members table and tracks which authenticated member uploaded this image. This is automatically captured from the authenticated session context and is never provided by the client in request bodies. The uploader information is used for permissions checking, audit trails, and attribution purposes.

url.description:
Download URL for accessing the actual image file.

This URL provides direct access to the stored image file, enabling users to view and download the image. Following AutoBE's URL-only file handling pattern, this field is CRITICAL for file access and must be included in all image attachment responses.

The URL is constructed from the stored_name field which contains the unique system-generated filename in the storage system (S3, CDN, or file server). It represents the complete, ready-to-use URL that clients can use immediately to display images inline in articles, provide download links in the user interface, enable full-resolution image viewing in modals or lightboxes, and implement image preloading for performance optimization.

Security considerations: The URL may be a signed URL with expiration for private content, or a public CDN URL for published article attachments. Access control is enforced at the URL generation level based on article visibility and user permissions. The URL should be treated as opaque by clients and not parsed or manipulated.

Without this URL field, clients have no way to access the actual image file content. The stored_name field alone is insufficient because it is an internal storage identifier, not a complete access path. This URL field is what enables the entire file download and display functionality in the discussion board system.

original_name.description:
Original filename of the uploaded image as provided by the user.

This is the filename that the user's file had when it was selected for upload (e.g., 'economic_chart_2024.png', 'trade_statistics.jpg'). The original filename is preserved for display purposes so users can identify their uploaded files easily. Maximum length is typically 255 characters to accommodate filesystem limitations.

stored_name.description:
Unique filename used for storage to prevent conflicts and ensure security.

This is the system-generated filename used to store the image file in the backend storage system. It is typically a UUID or hash-based name that ensures uniqueness and prevents filename collisions, path traversal attacks, and other security issues. This stored filename is never exposed to end users but is essential for internal file retrieval and management.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the image file for validation and proper content delivery.

Specifies the exact format of the image using standard MIME type notation. Valid values are 'image/jpeg' for JPEG/JPG images, 'image/png' for PNG images, 'image/gif' for GIF images, and 'image/webp' for WebP images. The MIME type is validated against both the file extension and actual file content to prevent format spoofing. This field is essential for setting proper Content-Type headers when serving images to browsers.

size_bytes.description:
File size in bytes.

The total size of the image file measured in bytes. This is validated during upload to ensure it does not exceed the 5MB (5,242,880 bytes) maximum limit for individual images. The size information is displayed to users alongside download links so they can make informed decisions about downloading files, particularly on metered or slow connections.

width.description:
Image width in pixels.

The horizontal dimension of the image in pixels. Used for validation during upload (minimum 50px, maximum 8000px) and for display optimization. The width information allows the system to generate appropriately sized thumbnails, apply responsive image techniques, and inform users about image dimensions before downloading or viewing full resolution versions.

height.description:
Image height in pixels.

The vertical dimension of the image in pixels. Used for validation during upload (minimum 50px, maximum 8000px) and for display optimization. Combined with width, this provides the complete aspect ratio of the image, enabling proper thumbnail generation, responsive display, and layout calculations in the article view.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the image was uploaded to the system.

Records the exact date and time when this image attachment was created and stored in the system. This timestamp is automatically set by the system during the upload operation and is immutable after creation. It is used for sorting attachments, tracking upload history, and audit trail purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the image was soft deleted.

When an image is removed by the article author or a moderator, this field is set to the deletion timestamp instead of permanently removing the database record. Null indicates the image is active and available. Soft deletion enables recovery if images are removed in error and maintains audit trails for moderation purposes. Images with non-null deleted_at are hidden from public view and treated as unavailable.

uploader.description:
Summary information about the member who uploaded this image attachment.

This relationship expansion provides identification of who added this visual supporting material to the article, including the uploader's username, display name, and basic profile information. This attribution is important for accountability, especially when images are added during article editing or when moderators enhance articles with additional visual evidence.

The uploader reference is derived from the uploaded_by_member_id foreign key, which points to the discussion_board_members table. The summary format prevents excessive nesting while providing essential user identification. This information helps readers understand content provenance and enables proper attribution of contributed visual materials.

For images uploaded during initial article creation, the uploader will be the same as the article author. For images added later through editing or by moderators enhancing content, the uploader may differ from the original article author. This distinction is valuable for tracking contributions and understanding content evolution over time.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.description:
Complete image attachment entity representing an uploaded image associated with a discussion board article.

This schema represents the full structure of an image attachment as stored in the discussion_board_article_images table. Image attachments serve as visual supporting evidence for economic and political discussions, enabling members to include charts, graphs, infographics, photographs, and other visual materials in their articles.

Every image attachment is permanently associated with a parent article through the discussion_board_article_id foreign key. When the parent article is deleted, all associated images are automatically removed through cascade deletion. Images are uploaded by members (tracked via uploaded_by_member_id) and support soft deletion through the deleted_at timestamp, allowing recovery and audit trail maintenance.

The schema captures both user-facing metadata (original filename, dimensions, file size) and internal storage details (stored filename, MIME type) necessary for secure file management. Image dimensions are validated during upload to ensure they meet minimum readable size (50x50 pixels) and do not exceed maximum practical size (8000x8000 pixels). File sizes are limited to 5MB per image to balance quality with storage and bandwidth considerations.

This response schema is returned when retrieving image details, after successful image uploads, and when listing article attachments. It provides clients with complete information needed for display, download, and management operations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the document attachment.

This is the primary key automatically generated by the system when a document is uploaded and attached to an article. It serves as the permanent reference for this specific document attachment throughout its lifecycle.

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Reference to the parent article this document is attached to.

This foreign key links the document to its parent article in the discussion_board_articles table. Every document attachment must belong to exactly one article. The relationship is enforced with cascade deletion - when an article is deleted, all its document attachments are automatically removed.

Kept as raw ID because this is a hierarchical parent FK - the parent article already contains this document in its documents array, so the child should not expand back to the parent to prevent circular references.

uploaded_by_member_id.description:
Reference to the member who uploaded this document attachment.

This foreign key tracks accountability for document uploads, linking to the discussion_board_members table. It records which user added this supporting material to the article, which is essential for moderation purposes and understanding content provenance. The uploader may be the article author or a moderator adding documentation to enhance the discussion.

original_name.description:
Original filename of the uploaded document as provided by the user.

This preserves the document's original name exactly as it appeared on the user's system (e.g., 'Federal_Reserve_Report_2024.pdf', 'Economic_Analysis.docx'). The original filename is displayed to users when viewing attachments and used as the default filename when downloading the document, maintaining familiarity and context for readers.

stored_name.description:
Unique filename used for internal storage to prevent conflicts and ensure security.

This is a system-generated filename (typically a UUID or hash-based name) used to store the file in the backend storage system. Using unique stored names prevents filename collisions when multiple users upload files with the same name, enhances security by obscuring actual file locations, and enables efficient file management. This field is for internal system use and typically not displayed to end users.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the document file for validation and proper content delivery.

Indicates the document format such as 'application/pdf' for PDF files, 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document' for DOCX files, 'application/msword' for DOC files, 'text/plain' for TXT files, 'application/rtf' for RTF files, or 'application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text' for ODT files. This information is used to validate that the uploaded file matches supported formats, set appropriate HTTP Content-Type headers when serving the file, and help browsers handle the file correctly (inline viewing for PDFs, download prompt for Word documents, etc.).

size_bytes.description:
File size in bytes of the document attachment.

Represents the exact size of the document file stored in the system. This value is used to enforce the maximum file size limit of 10MB (10,485,760 bytes) per document during upload validation, calculate total attachment size to enforce the 100MB limit per article, and display file size information to users before they download documents (helping users make informed decisions about downloads, especially on limited bandwidth connections). The size is measured in bytes for precision.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the document was uploaded to the system.

Automatically recorded when the document attachment record is created in the database. This timestamp indicates when the document was added to the article, which may be during initial article creation or later through editing. The timestamp is displayed to users to provide context about when supporting materials were added and is used for sorting attachments chronologically in article views.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete timestamp marking when the document was removed from the article.

When a document is deleted (by the article author, moderator, or through article deletion), this field is set to the deletion timestamp rather than permanently removing the record. Null indicates the document is currently active and accessible. Soft deletion enables audit trails for moderation actions, potential recovery of accidentally deleted documents, and maintaining referential integrity in moderation logs. Soft-deleted documents are excluded from normal queries and not accessible to regular users, but moderators may view them for audit purposes.

uploader.description:
Summary information about the member who uploaded this document attachment.

Provides identification of who added this supporting material to the article, including the uploader's username, display name, and basic profile information. This attribution is important for accountability, especially when documents are added by moderators during content enhancement or when multiple contributors work on an article. The summary format prevents excessive nesting while providing essential user identification.

IDiscussionBoardArticleDocument.description:
Complete representation of a document attachment within a discussion board article.

This entity represents document files (PDF, DOCX, DOC, TXT, RTF, ODT) that members attach to their articles as supporting evidence, research papers, policy documents, or reference materials for economic and political discussions. Document attachments enhance articles by providing downloadable resources that readers can review for detailed information, data, or primary sources.

Each document attachment maintains comprehensive metadata including the original filename for user display, a unique stored filename for secure internal storage, MIME type for proper content delivery, file size for user information and validation, upload tracking information, and soft deletion support for audit trails. The entity tracks both the article it belongs to (via discussion_board_article_id) and the member who uploaded it (via uploader reference), enabling proper access control and accountability.

Document attachments are subject to validation rules including maximum 10MB per document file, maximum 5 document attachments per article, total attachment limit of 100MB per article (combined images and documents), and allowed formats limited to PDF, Word documents, and text-based formats. The system validates files by both MIME type and actual content to prevent format spoofing.

This entity supports the core platform value proposition of evidence-based discussion by enabling users to attach authoritative documents directly to their articles, making supporting materials immediately accessible without requiring external links or separate hosting. Documents are displayed as downloadable links with file metadata, helping readers access and verify the evidence underlying article claims.

title.description:
Updated article title or headline.

The article title must be between 5 and 200 characters long. When updating the title, the system validates length constraints and ensures the title contains meaningful content rather than only whitespace or special characters. The updated title will be reflected in all article listings and the article detail page.

body.description:
Updated main article content and body text.

The full text content of the article must be between 20 and 50,000 characters. When updating the body, the system preserves paragraph breaks and basic formatting while sanitizing HTML input to prevent security vulnerabilities. The updated content becomes the current version of the article.

summary.description:
Updated article excerpt or summary.

An optional brief summary or excerpt, limited to 500 characters maximum. This field can be updated to provide a better preview for article listings and search results. Setting this to null removes any existing summary.

oneOf.description:
Updated publication status of the article.

Changes the article's lifecycle state. Transitioning from 'published' to 'draft' removes the article from public view. Changing to 'archived' moves the article out of primary circulation. Only published articles appear in standard listings and search results.

Updated publication status of the article.

Changes the article's lifecycle state. Transitioning from 'published' to 'draft' removes the article from public view. Changing to 'archived' moves the article out of primary circulation. Only published articles appear in standard listings and search results.

Updated publication status of the article.

Changes the article's lifecycle state. Transitioning from 'published' to 'draft' removes the article from public view. Changing to 'archived' moves the article out of primary circulation. Only published articles appear in standard listings and search results.

status.description:
Updated publication status of the article.

Changes the article's lifecycle state. Transitioning from 'published' to 'draft' removes the article from public view. Changing to 'archived' moves the article out of primary circulation. Only published articles appear in standard listings and search results.

category_ids.description:
Updated category associations for this article.

Array of category IDs from the discussion_board_categories table to classify this article's subject matter. Articles must have at least one category. When updating, the system replaces all existing category associations (via discussion_board_article_categories junction table) with the new set of categories provided.

tag_ids.description:
Updated tag associations for this article.

Array of tag IDs from the discussion_board_tags table providing granular topic keywords. Maximum 5 tags allowed per article. When updating, the system replaces all existing tag associations (via discussion_board_article_tags junction table) with the new set of tags. This field is optional and can be an empty array to remove all tags.

add_image_ids.description:
Image attachments to add to the article.

Array of image IDs from the discussion_board_article_images table to attach to this article. The system validates that adding these images will not exceed the maximum limit of 10 images per article. Each referenced image must exist and must not already be associated with another article.

remove_image_ids.description:
Image attachments to remove from the article.

Array of image IDs currently associated with this article that should be removed. The system soft-deletes these images by setting their deleted_at timestamp, removing them from the article view while preserving records for audit purposes. Removed images are deleted from file storage.

add_document_ids.description:
Document attachments to add to the article.

Array of document IDs from the discussion_board_article_documents table to attach to this article. The system validates that adding these documents will not exceed the maximum limit of 5 documents per article. Each referenced document must exist and must not already be associated with another article.

remove_document_ids.description:
Document attachments to remove from the article.

Array of document IDs currently associated with this article that should be removed. The system soft-deletes these documents by setting their deleted_at timestamp, removing them from the article view while preserving records for audit purposes. Removed documents are deleted from file storage.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description:
Update request for modifying an existing discussion board article.

This type defines the structure for article update operations, allowing modification of article content, metadata, categorization, and attachment management. All fields are optional, enabling partial updates where only specific aspects of the article are changed. The operation enforces strict ownership validation ensuring only the original author or moderators can update articles.

When an article is updated, the system creates a snapshot in the discussion_board_article_snapshots table to preserve the previous version for audit trail and version control purposes. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time while preserving the immutable created_at timestamp.

Content updates support modifying the title (5-200 characters), body text (20-50,000 characters), and optional summary (max 500 characters). All text content is validated and sanitized to prevent security vulnerabilities while preserving user-intended formatting.

Categorization updates allow reassigning articles to different categories by providing a new set of category IDs. The system validates that all referenced categories exist in the discussion_board_categories table and maintains the many-to-many relationship through the discussion_board_article_categories junction table. At least one category must be assigned.

Tag updates enable adding, removing, or replacing tags by providing a new set of tag IDs. Maximum 5 tags are allowed per article. The system validates tag references against the discussion_board_tags table and manages associations through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table.

Attachment management supports independent addition and removal of images and documents through separate array fields. When adding attachments, the system validates against maximum limits (10 images, 5 documents) including existing attachments. When removing attachments, the system soft-deletes the referenced files by setting deleted_at timestamps and cleans up storage resources.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve in the paginated response. Page numbering starts at 1 for the first page. When combined with limit, this determines the offset for result retrieval.

Must be a positive integer. Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description:
Number of items per page.

Specifies how many image attachment records to return in a single page of results. This controls the page size for pagination and affects response payload size and loading performance.

Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20 if not specified. Lower values improve initial response time, while higher values reduce the number of requests needed to retrieve all results.

search.description:
Keyword search term for filtering images.

Searches across image metadata fields including original filename. Enables users to find specific images by name or keyword. Search is case-insensitive and supports partial matching.

Optional parameter. When not provided, no keyword filtering is applied.

mime_type.description:
Filter by specific MIME type.

Restricts results to images with the specified MIME type such as image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, or image/webp. Enables filtering by image format.

Optional parameter. When not provided, all supported image formats are included in results.

min_width.description:
Minimum image width in pixels.

Filters results to include only images with width greater than or equal to this value. Useful for finding images of sufficient resolution for specific display purposes.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided.

max_width.description:
Maximum image width in pixels.

Filters results to include only images with width less than or equal to this value. Useful for finding smaller images or excluding very large images.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided. Should be greater than min_width if both are specified.

min_height.description:
Minimum image height in pixels.

Filters results to include only images with height greater than or equal to this value. Useful for finding images of sufficient resolution for specific display purposes.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided.

max_height.description:
Maximum image height in pixels.

Filters results to include only images with height less than or equal to this value. Useful for finding smaller images or excluding very large images.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided. Should be greater than min_height if both are specified.

min_size_bytes.description:
Minimum file size in bytes.

Filters results to include only images with file size greater than or equal to this value. Useful for finding higher quality images or excluding very small images.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided.

max_size_bytes.description:
Maximum file size in bytes.

Filters results to include only images with file size less than or equal to this value. Useful for finding smaller images or excluding very large images. Cannot exceed 5MB (5,242,880 bytes), which is the system maximum for individual image files.

Optional parameter. Must be a non-negative integer if provided. Should be greater than min_size_bytes if both are specified.

uploaded_after.description:
Filter images uploaded after this timestamp.

Restricts results to images with created_at timestamp after the specified date and time. Useful for finding recently added images or images added within a specific timeframe.
