   * members and moderators can access the profile. When set to 'private', only
   * moderators can view the profile for moderation purposes.
   *
   * Security considerations include protecting private information such as
   * email addresses, password hashes, and internal metadata from unauthorized
   * access. The operation enforces role-based access control based on the
   * requesting user's authentication status and actor type. Email addresses are
   * never exposed in public profile responses and are only visible to the
   * profile owner and moderators. The response includes only information
   * appropriate for the requesting user's authorization level.
   *
   * This operation integrates with the discussion_board_members table as
   * defined in the Prisma schema, utilizing fields including username,
   * display_name, bio, location, website_url, profile_picture_url,
   * profile_visibility, activity_visibility, created_at, last_login_at, and
   * soft delete tracking via deleted_at. The operation excludes soft-deleted
   * members where deleted_at is not null, ensuring deleted accounts are not
   * accessible.
   *
   * Related API operations include PATCH /members for searching and listing
   * member profiles, PUT /members/{memberUsername} for updating the
   * authenticated user's own profile, and various article and comment endpoints
   * that reference member profiles through authorship attribution.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param memberUsername Unique username identifier of the target member whose
   *   profile is being retrieved (global scope)
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Get(":memberUsername")
  public async at(
    @TypedParam("memberUsername")
    memberUsername: string,
  ): Promise<IDiscussionBoardMember> {
    try {
      return await getDiscussionBoardMembersMemberUsername({
        memberUsername,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}

import { Controller } from "@nestjs/common";
import { TypedRoute, TypedBody, TypedParam } from "@nestia/core";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";
import { postDiscussionBoardMemberArticles } from "../../../../providers/postDiscussionBoardMemberArticles";
import { MemberAuth } from "../../../../decorators/MemberAuth";
import { MemberPayload } from "../../../../decorators/payload/MemberPayload";
import { putDiscussionBoardMemberArticlesArticleId } from "../../../../providers/putDiscussionBoardMemberArticlesArticleId";
import { deleteDiscussionBoardMemberArticlesArticleId } from "../../../../providers/deleteDiscussionBoardMemberArticlesArticleId";

import { IDiscussionBoardArticle } from "../../../../api/structures/IDiscussionBoardArticle";

@Controller("/discussionBoard/member/articles")
export class DiscussionboardMemberArticlesController {
  /**
   * Create and publish a new discussion board article as a member.
   *
   * Create a new article in the discussion board system for sharing economic
   * and political analysis, commentary, and discussions. This operation allows
   * authenticated members to publish content with rich text formatting,
   * categorization, tagging, and multimedia attachments including images and
   * documents.
   *
   * The article creation process validates all required fields according to
   * business rules defined in the requirements. The title must be between 5 and
   * 200 characters, providing enough space for descriptive headlines while
   * preventing excessive length. The body content must be between 20 and 50,000
   * characters, ensuring substantive content while preventing abuse. The system
   * requires selection of at least one category from predefined economic and
   * political topic categories (stored in discussion_board_categories), and
   * supports up to 5 optional tags (from discussion_board_tags) for enhanced
   * discoverability.
   *
   * Attachment support enables evidence-based discussions by allowing members
   * to upload supporting materials. Articles can include up to 10 image
   * attachments (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP formats, maximum 5MB each) for charts,
   * graphs, infographics, and visual evidence, as well as up to 5 document
   * attachments (PDF, DOCX, DOC, TXT, RTF, ODT formats, maximum 10MB each) for
   * research papers, policy documents, and supplementary materials. The total
   * attachment size across all files is limited to 50MB per article to balance
   * functionality with storage and performance considerations.
   *
   * Upon successful creation, the system sets the article status to
   * 'published', initializes view_count and comment_count to 0, assigns the
   * authenticated member as the author in the discussion_board_member_id field,
   * and records the creation timestamp. The operation returns the complete
   * article entity including the system-generated article ID, allowing the
   * client to navigate to the newly published article.
   *
   * Security and data integrity measures include authentication verification to
   * ensure only logged-in members can create articles, input sanitization to
   * prevent XSS attacks while preserving formatting, validation of category and
   * tag references against the discussion_board_categories and
   * discussion_board_tags tables, file upload validation including type
   * checking, size limits, and malware scanning, and rate limiting to prevent
   * spam or automated article creation abuse.
   *
   * This operation integrates with multiple system components including the
   * user authentication system to verify member identity, the file storage
   * system to handle image and document uploads
   * (discussion_board_article_images and discussion_board_article_documents
   * tables), the category and tag systems for content organization
   * (discussion_board_article_categories and discussion_board_article_tags
   * junction tables), and the snapshot system which creates an initial version
   * record in discussion_board_article_snapshots for audit trail purposes.
   *
   * Related operations include the article search endpoint (PATCH /articles)
   * for discovering existing content before posting to avoid duplicates, the
   * article detail endpoint (GET /articles/{articleId}) for viewing the newly
   * published article, and the article update endpoint (PUT
   * /articles/{articleId}) for editing the article after publication if
   * corrections are needed.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Article creation data including title, body content, category,
   *   optional tags, optional summary, and attachment references
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Post()
  public async create(
    @MemberAuth()
    member: MemberPayload,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate,
  ): Promise<IDiscussionBoardArticle> {
    try {
      return await postDiscussionBoardMemberArticles({
        member,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Update an existing article with new content and metadata.
   *
   * Update the content and metadata of an existing article in the discussion
   * board system. This operation allows article authors to modify their
   * published articles by updating the title, body content, summary,
   * publication status, associated categories, tags, and managing image and
   * document attachments. The operation enforces strict ownership validation
   * ensuring that only the original author (identified by
   * discussion_board_member_id) can update their own articles, unless the
   * requesting user is a moderator who possesses elevated permissions to edit
   * any article regardless of authorship.
   *
   * The update process validates all input fields according to the business
   * rules defined in the requirements. Article titles must be between 5 and 200
   * characters, body content must be between 20 and 50,000 characters,
   * summaries are optional with a maximum of 500 characters, and up to 5 tags
   * can be applied with each tag being 2-30 characters. The system validates
   * that selected categories exist in the discussion_board_categories table and
   * that tags conform to the normalized lowercase format defined in the
   * discussion_board_tags table.
   *
   * When a member successfully updates their article, the system creates a new
   * record in the discussion_board_article_snapshots table to preserve the
   * previous version for version control and audit purposes. This snapshot
   * includes the complete article state before the update including title,
   * body, summary, and status fields along with a timestamp marking when this
   * version existed. The created_by_member_id in the snapshot references the
   * member who made the update.
   *
   * Attachment management during article updates supports adding new images and
   * documents up to the defined limits (10 images maximum, 5 documents maximum,
   * with individual file size limits of 5MB for images and 10MB for documents).
   * When attachments are removed during an edit, the system marks the
   * corresponding records in discussion_board_article_images or
   * discussion_board_article_documents with a deleted_at timestamp following
   * the soft deletion pattern. The system enforces total attachment limits
   * including both existing and newly added files.
   *
   * The operation automatically updates the updated_at timestamp to the current
   * time, preserving the original created_at timestamp as an immutable
   * historical record. If a moderator performs the update, the
   * last_modified_by_moderator_id field is set to the moderator's ID to track
   * moderator intervention in the content. The view_count and comment_count
   * fields are not modified by this operation as they are system-managed
   * metrics updated through separate processes.
   *
   * This endpoint respects the soft deletion mechanism in the schema. If the
   * article has a non-null deleted_at timestamp, the article is considered
   * deleted and the update operation returns a 404 Not Found error. Only active
   * articles (deleted_at is null) can be updated through this endpoint.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param articleId Unique identifier of the target article to update
   * @param body Updated article content and metadata including title, body,
   *   summary, categories, tags, and attachment management instructions
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Put(":articleId")
  public async update(
    @MemberAuth()
    member: MemberPayload,
    @TypedParam("articleId")
    articleId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate,
  ): Promise<IDiscussionBoardArticle> {
    try {
      return await putDiscussionBoardMemberArticlesArticleId({
        member,
        articleId,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Mark an article as deleted while preserving it for audit and potential
   * recovery.
   *
   * This operation marks an article as deleted in the discussion board system
   * by setting the deleted_at timestamp, while preserving all article data and
   * relationships in the database for audit trail purposes and potential
   * recovery. This follows the soft delete pattern defined in the Prisma schema
   * for the discussion_board_articles table.
   *
   * When an article is soft deleted, the system sets the deleted_at field to
   * the current timestamp. This timestamp acts as a marker that the article has
   * been deleted, causing it to be filtered out from public article listings,
   * search results, and normal browsing interfaces. However, the complete
   * article record remains in the database with all its content, metadata, and
   * relationships intact. This preservation is essential for maintaining
   * discussion context, enabling content recovery if deletion was accidental or
   * incorrect, supporting moderation audit trails, and complying with data
   * retention requirements.
   *
   * The soft deletion process affects related data in a coordinated manner.
   * Comments posted on the article (discussion_board_comments) are typically
   * also soft deleted by setting their deleted_at timestamps, hiding the entire
   * discussion thread from public view while preserving it for audit purposes.
   * Historical article snapshots (discussion_board_article_snapshots) are
   * retained unchanged since they represent historical versions and serve as
   * permanent audit records. Category associations
   * (discussion_board_article_categories) and tag associations
   * (discussion_board_article_tags) may be removed or retained based on
   * implementation strategy. Image attachments
   * (discussion_board_article_images) and document attachments
   * (discussion_board_article_documents) are typically soft deleted by setting
   * their deleted_at fields, hiding them from public access while preserving
   * file metadata and enabling potential restoration.
   *
   * From a security and permissions perspective, this operation can be
   * performed by two types of users. The original article author (identified by
   * discussion_board_member_id in the article record) has the right to delete
   * their own articles at any time after publication. Additionally, any
   * moderator has the authority to delete any article regardless of authorship
   * as part of content moderation responsibilities. The system enforces these
   * permissions by verifying either ownership match or moderator role before
   * allowing the deletion to proceed. When a moderator deletes another user's
   * article, the action should be logged in the
   * discussion_board_moderation_actions table with action_type set to
   * delete_content, creating a complete audit trail of the moderation
   * intervention.
   *
   * This operation supports content recovery and audit capabilities. Because
   * soft deleted articles remain in the database with all their data intact,
   * moderators or the original author can potentially restore the article by
   * clearing or nullifying the deleted_at timestamp. The article and all its
   * associated content can be brought back to public visibility if the deletion
   * was performed in error or if review determines the content does not violate
   * guidelines. This recovery capability is a key advantage of soft deletion
   * over hard deletion. Users should still be prompted for confirmation before
   * deletion is executed to prevent accidental deletions, even though soft
   * deletion is reversible.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param articleId Unique identifier of the target article to be marked as
   *   deleted
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Delete(":articleId")
  public async erase(
    @MemberAuth()
    member: MemberPayload,
    @TypedParam("articleId")
    articleId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
  ): Promise<void> {
    try {
      return await deleteDiscussionBoardMemberArticlesArticleId({
        member,
        articleId,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}

   * moderators to upload supporting materials. Articles can include up to 10
   * image attachments (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP formats, maximum 5MB each) for
   * charts, graphs, infographics, and visual evidence, as well as up to 5
   * document attachments (PDF, DOCX, DOC, TXT, RTF, ODT formats, maximum 10MB
   * each) for research papers, policy documents, and supplementary materials.
   * The total attachment size across all files is limited to 50MB per article
   * to balance functionality with storage and performance considerations.
   *
   * Upon successful creation, the system sets the article status to
   * 'published', initializes view_count and comment_count to 0, records the
   * creation timestamp, and handles moderator authorship according to the
   * schema design. The moderator's identity is tracked for accountability and
   * moderation audit purposes. The operation returns the complete article
   * entity including the system-generated article ID, allowing the client to
   * navigate to the newly published article.
   *
   * Security and data integrity measures include authentication verification to
   * ensure only logged-in moderators can access this endpoint, input
   * sanitization to prevent XSS attacks while preserving formatting, validation
   * of category and tag references against the discussion_board_categories and
   * discussion_board_tags tables, file upload validation including type
   * checking, size limits, and malware scanning, and comprehensive audit
   * logging of moderator content creation for transparency and accountability.
   *
   * This operation integrates with multiple system components including the
   * user authentication system to verify moderator identity, the file storage
   * system to handle image and document uploads
   * (discussion_board_article_images and discussion_board_article_documents
   * tables), the category and tag systems for content organization
   * (discussion_board_article_categories and discussion_board_article_tags
   * junction tables), the snapshot system which creates an initial version
   * record in discussion_board_article_snapshots for audit trail purposes, and
   * the moderation system which may log this action in
   * discussion_board_moderation_actions for oversight.
   *
   * Related operations include the article search endpoint (PATCH /articles)
   * for discovering existing content, the article detail endpoint (GET
   * /articles/{articleId}) for viewing the newly published article, the article
   * update endpoint (PUT /articles/{articleId}) for editing the article after
   * publication, and member article creation (POST /member/articles) which
   * provides similar functionality for regular members.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Article creation data including title, body content, category,
   *   optional tags, optional summary, and attachment references
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Post()
  public async create(
    @ModeratorAuth()
    moderator: ModeratorPayload,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate,
  ): Promise<IDiscussionBoardArticle> {
    try {
      return await postDiscussionBoardModeratorArticles({
        moderator,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Mark an article as deleted while preserving it for audit and potential
   * recovery.
   *
   * This operation marks an article as deleted in the discussion board system
   * by setting the deleted_at timestamp, while preserving all article data and
   * relationships in the database for audit trail purposes and potential
   * recovery. This follows the soft delete pattern defined in the Prisma schema
   * for the discussion_board_articles table.
   *
   * When an article is soft deleted, the system sets the deleted_at field to
   * the current timestamp. This timestamp acts as a marker that the article has
   * been deleted, causing it to be filtered out from public article listings,
   * search results, and normal browsing interfaces. However, the complete
   * article record remains in the database with all its content, metadata, and
   * relationships intact. This preservation is essential for maintaining
   * discussion context, enabling content recovery if deletion was accidental or
   * incorrect, supporting moderation audit trails, and complying with data
   * retention requirements.
   *
   * The soft deletion process affects related data in a coordinated manner.
   * Comments posted on the article (discussion_board_comments) are typically
   * also soft deleted by setting their deleted_at timestamps, hiding the entire
   * discussion thread from public view while preserving it for audit purposes.
   * Historical article snapshots (discussion_board_article_snapshots) are
   * retained unchanged since they represent historical versions and serve as
   * permanent audit records. Category associations
   * (discussion_board_article_categories) and tag associations
   * (discussion_board_article_tags) may be removed or retained based on
   * implementation strategy. Image attachments
   * (discussion_board_article_images) and document attachments
   * (discussion_board_article_documents) are typically soft deleted by setting
   * their deleted_at fields, hiding them from public access while preserving
   * file metadata and enabling potential restoration.
   *
   * From a security and permissions perspective, this operation can be
   * performed by two types of users. The original article author (identified by
   * discussion_board_member_id in the article record) has the right to delete
   * their own articles at any time after publication. Additionally, any
   * moderator has the authority to delete any article regardless of authorship
   * as part of content moderation responsibilities. The system enforces these
   * permissions by verifying either ownership match or moderator role before
   * allowing the deletion to proceed. When a moderator deletes another user's
   * article, the action should be logged in the
   * discussion_board_moderation_actions table with action_type set to
   * delete_content, creating a complete audit trail of the moderation
   * intervention.
   *
   * This operation supports content recovery and audit capabilities. Because
   * soft deleted articles remain in the database with all their data intact,
   * moderators or the original author can potentially restore the article by
   * clearing or nullifying the deleted_at timestamp. The article and all its
   * associated content can be brought back to public visibility if the deletion
   * was performed in error or if review determines the content does not violate
   * guidelines. This recovery capability is a key advantage of soft deletion
   * over hard deletion. Users should still be prompted for confirmation before
   * deletion is executed to prevent accidental deletions, even though soft
   * deletion is reversible.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param articleId Unique identifier of the target article to be marked as
   *   deleted
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Delete(":articleId")
  public async erase(
    @ModeratorAuth()
    moderator: ModeratorPayload,
    @TypedParam("articleId")
    articleId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
  ): Promise<void> {
    try {
      return await deleteDiscussionBoardModeratorArticlesArticleId({
        moderator,
        articleId,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}

import { Controller } from "@nestjs/common";
import { TypedRoute, TypedBody } from "@nestia/core";
import typia from "typia";
import { patchDiscussionBoardSearchArticles } from "../../../../providers/patchDiscussionBoardSearchArticles";

import { IPageIDiscussionBoardArticle } from "../../../../api/structures/IPageIDiscussionBoardArticle";
import { IDiscussionBoardArticle } from "../../../../api/structures/IDiscussionBoardArticle";

@Controller("/discussionBoard/search/articles")
export class DiscussionboardSearchArticlesController {
  /**
   * Search and retrieve filtered, paginated list of discussion board articles.
   *
   * Retrieve a comprehensive, filtered, and paginated list of discussion board
   * articles based on advanced search criteria. This operation enables users to
   * discover relevant economic and political discussions through keyword
   * search, category filtering, tag filtering, author filtering, and date range
   * constraints.
   *
   * The search functionality performs full-text search across article titles
   * and body content using PostgreSQL trigram indexes for efficient partial
   * matching. Users can search for keywords like "monetary policy" or "trade
   * agreements" and receive ranked results based on relevance. The system
   * prioritizes title matches over body content matches to surface the most
   * relevant articles.
   *
   * This operation supports comprehensive filtering options including multiple
   * category selection (articles matching any selected category), multiple tag
   * selection (articles matching all selected tags), author filtering by member
   * username, date range filtering for publication dates, and attachment
   * presence filtering (articles with images, documents, or any attachments).
   * Filters can be combined to create highly specific queries.
   *
   * Sorting capabilities include multiple options: relevance-based ranking for
   * keyword searches (default when search keywords are provided), newest first
   * by creation date (default when no keywords), oldest first, most viewed by
   * view_count, most commented by comment_count, and recently updated by
   * updated_at timestamp. The system maintains consistent performance even with
   * complex filter and sort combinations through appropriate database
   * indexing.
   *
   * Pagination follows standard patterns with configurable page size (10, 20,
   * 50, or 100 articles per page, default 20) and page number navigation.
   * Results include total article count, total page count, current page number,
   * and the array of matching articles in summary format optimized for list
   * display.
   *
   * Security considerations include rate limiting on search operations to
   * prevent abuse, filtering out soft-deleted articles (where deleted_at is not
   * null), respecting article status (only published articles visible to
   * guests, draft articles visible only to authors), and appropriate access
   * control based on the requesting user's authentication status. The operation
   * is accessible to all users including guests, members, and moderators, with
   * identical search capabilities for all user types.
   *
   * This operation integrates with the discussion_board_articles table as the
   * primary data source, joins with discussion_board_article_categories and
   * discussion_board_categories for category filtering, joins with
   * discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags for tag filtering,
   * joins with discussion_board_members for author information, and references
   * discussion_board_article_images and discussion_board_article_documents for
   * attachment filtering. The response returns summary information optimized
   * for search result display, including article metadata, excerpt from body
   * content, author information, category and tag lists, and attachment
   * indicators without loading full attachment details.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Search criteria including keywords, filters, sorting
   *   preferences, and pagination parameters for article discovery
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Patch()
  public async search(
    @TypedBody()
    body: IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest,
  ): Promise<IPageIDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary> {
    try {
      return await patchDiscussionBoardSearchArticles({
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}

import { Controller } from "@nestjs/common";
import { TypedRoute } from "@nestia/core";
import typia from "typia";
import { getDiscussionBoardModeratorModerationDashboardOverview } from "../../../../../providers/getDiscussionBoardModeratorModerationDashboardOverview";
import { ModeratorAuth } from "../../../../../decorators/ModeratorAuth";
import { ModeratorPayload } from "../../../../../decorators/payload/ModeratorPayload";
import { getDiscussionBoardModeratorModerationDashboardStatistics } from "../../../../../providers/getDiscussionBoardModeratorModerationDashboardStatistics";

import { IDiscussionBoardModerationDashboardOverview } from "../../../../../api/structures/IDiscussionBoardModerationDashboardOverview";
import { IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics } from "../../../../../api/structures/IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics";

@Controller("/discussionBoard/moderator/moderation/dashboard")
export class DiscussionboardModeratorModerationDashboardController {
  /**
   * Retrieve comprehensive moderation dashboard overview with pending reports
   * and recent activity.
   *
   * This operation provides moderators with a comprehensive overview of the
   * moderation dashboard, consolidating critical information from multiple data
   * sources to enable efficient moderation workflows. The dashboard overview
   * serves as the primary entry point for moderators to assess current
   * moderation needs and prioritize their work.
   *
   * The overview includes several key components that give moderators complete
   * situational awareness. First, it displays all pending reports that require
   * review, including both article and comment reports that members have
   * flagged for potential guideline violations. Each pending report shows
   * essential metadata such as report reason, submission time, and number of
   * reports on the same content to help moderators prioritize urgent issues.
   * Second, the overview presents recent moderation actions taken by all
   * moderators, creating transparency and enabling team coordination. This
   * includes content edits, deletions, user warnings, and suspensions with
   * timestamps and brief descriptions. Third, it shows currently active user
   * suspensions that are in effect, helping moderators track enforcement
   * actions and upcoming expiration dates.
   *
   * The dashboard aggregates statistics across the moderation system to provide
   * quantitative insights into moderation workload and trends. Key metrics
   * include total pending reports awaiting review, reports currently under
   * review by other moderators, reports resolved in the past 24 hours, total
   * active suspensions in effect, and warnings issued in the past week. These
   * statistics help moderators understand system health and identify patterns
   * that may require policy adjustments or additional moderator resources.
   *
   * Security considerations include strict authorization enforcement ensuring
   * only authenticated moderators can access this endpoint. The operation
   * respects moderator permissions as defined in the
   * discussion_board_moderators table, where the moderation_permissions field
   * may specify different access levels for different moderator roles. The
   * dashboard data is sensitive and contains information about reported content
   * and user enforcement actions that must not be exposed to regular members or
   * guests.
   *
   * This operation integrates data from the discussion_board_reports table to
   * show pending and recent reports, the discussion_board_moderation_actions
   * table to display recent moderator interventions, the
   * discussion_board_user_warnings table to count recent warnings, and the
   * discussion_board_user_suspensions table to show active suspensions. The
   * response provides a unified view of this distributed data, optimized for
   * quick assessment and decision-making by moderators who need to efficiently
   * manage community content quality.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Get("overview")
  public async overview(
    @ModeratorAuth()
    moderator: ModeratorPayload,
  ): Promise<IDiscussionBoardModerationDashboardOverview> {
    try {
      return await getDiscussionBoardModeratorModerationDashboardOverview({
        moderator,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Retrieve detailed moderation statistics and analytics for system health
   * monitoring.
   *
   * This operation provides moderators with detailed statistical analysis of
   * moderation activity and system health metrics. The statistics endpoint goes
   * beyond the basic overview to deliver comprehensive analytics that help
   * moderators understand trends, measure effectiveness, and identify areas
   * requiring attention. This data-driven approach to moderation enables
   * informed decision-making about policy enforcement and resource allocation.
   *
   * The statistics response includes several analytical dimensions that provide
   * deep insight into moderation patterns. Time-series data shows how report
   * volumes, moderation actions, and enforcement decisions have changed over
   * various time periods including the past 24 hours, past week, and past
   * month. This temporal analysis helps identify emerging issues, seasonal
   * patterns, or trending topics that may require increased moderation
   * attention. Breakdown by violation type categorizes reports and actions by
   * the type of guideline violation such as spam, harassment, misinformation,
   * and offensive content, enabling moderators to understand which policy areas
   * see the most activity and may need clearer guidelines or additional
   * enforcement focus.
   *
   * Moderator workload distribution shows how moderation work is distributed
   * across the moderator team, including reports reviewed per moderator,
   * average review time per report, and actions taken per moderator. This helps
   * identify workload balance issues and recognize particularly active or
   * effective moderators. Resolution outcome statistics track how reports are
   * resolved including percentage dismissed as false reports, percentage
   * resulting in content edits, percentage resulting in content deletion, and
   * percentage resulting in user warnings or suspensions. These metrics measure
   * the accuracy of community reporting and the appropriateness of moderation
   * responses.
   *
   * User behavior metrics analyze patterns in user violations and enforcement
   * effectiveness. Statistics include repeat violation rates showing what
   * percentage of warned or suspended users commit subsequent violations, time
   * between violations for users with multiple infractions, and effectiveness
   * of progressive discipline in reducing problematic behavior. Content health
   * metrics measure overall community quality including ratio of reported
   * content to total content, average time to resolve reports, and percentage
   * of content requiring moderation intervention.
   *
   * The operation calculates aggregations and percentages from raw data in the
   * underlying tables, including GROUP BY operations on time periods and
   * violation categories, COUNT and SUM aggregations for various metrics, and
   * AVERAGE calculations for response times and resolution rates. The
   * statistics do not map to a single Prisma table but instead represent
   * computed analytical views derived from multiple tables through complex SQL
   * queries and business logic.
   *
   * Security and authorization requirements ensure only authenticated
   * moderators can access these statistics. The data contains sensitive
   * information about enforcement actions and community health that must be
   * restricted to users with moderation privileges. The response does not
   * include personally identifiable information about specific users but
   * provides aggregate anonymous statistics suitable for system monitoring and
   * policy evaluation.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Get("statistics")
  public async statistics(
    @ModeratorAuth()
    moderator: ModeratorPayload,
  ): Promise<IDiscussionBoardModerationStatistics> {
    try {
      return await getDiscussionBoardModeratorModerationDashboardStatistics({
        moderator,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}
